sections.h2: Where is New Britain and what is it known for?
sections.html:
New Britain is a city in Hartford County, about 9 miles southwest of Hartford, and it is part of the Capitol Planning Region. The 2020 census counted 74,135 residents in about 13.4 square miles, almost all of it land.

The area was settled in 1687 and organized as the New Britain Society parish in 1754. It was chartered as a town in 1850 and a city in 1871, separating from Farmington and Berlin, and a consolidation charter followed in 1905. The nickname Hardware City comes from the factories that once made locks, tools and hardware here. Stanley Black & Decker is still headquartered in the city.

The terrain is gentle, rolling hills with many street trees, and Walnut Hill Park was designed by Frederick Law Olmsted.

sections.h2: What are the biggest employers in New Britain?
sections.html:
Central Connecticut State University is the largest employer in New Britain, with 2,879 people, according to the city's 2024 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report as cited on Wikipedia.

1Central Connecticut State University2,879

3City of New Britain1,910
4Hospital for Special Care1,300

Other headquarters in the city include Gaffney, Bennett and Associates, Tomasso Group, Creed Monarch, Guida's Dairy and Polamer Precision. The university, the two hospitals and city government account for more than 8,600 of the jobs in that top-five list.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about New Britain homes and households?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 29,054 households and 31,510 housing units in New Britain, with 7.8 percent of the units vacant. About a third of households were one person living alone. The median age was 34.6 years.

Wikipedia reports a 2021 median household income of $51,586 and a poverty rate of 19.9 percent. The Census survey figures we use elsewhere on this page show renters in about 56 percent of occupied homes and a median build year of 1956. Put together, those facts describe a city of older houses, many of them rented. Sellers who inherit a two-family or a house with tenants are common here, and tenant-occupied sales raise their own questions about access, repairs and timing.

  • Older wiring and plumbing are common in houses built around 1956.
  • A tenant-occupied house may need written notice before showings.
  • A probate sale can take longer than a standard sale.

Ask your attorney how each issue applies to your house, and ask the Assessor whether any recent permit or addition changed the assessed value.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in New Britain?
sections.html:
The city's Assessor sets assessments and its Tax Collector bills and collects the tax. The Tax Collector's pages cover online tax payments, and the city's website is newbritainct.gov.

QuestionWho answers it
What is my assessed value?City Assessor
What do I owe and when?City Tax Collector
How do I pay online?Online Tax Payments page
What happens if I cannot pay?Ask the Tax Collector first

Please call the office or read your bill for exact installment dates and interest. Connecticut law, not the city, sets the legal framework, and the General Assembly's Chapter 204 covers how taxes are levied and collected.

sections.h2: What state options exist if you cannot pay New Britain tax?
sections.html:
Connecticut gives cities a few tools for owners who struggle with the bill. Section 12-124 lets a city's mayor and aldermen abate taxes or the interest on delinquent taxes for persons who are poor and unable to pay, with the approval of a standing abatement committee or the state's Secretary of the Office of Policy and Management.

Section 12-124a lets a municipality abate tax that exceeds 8 percent of an owner-occupant's income, but only if the owner signs a reimbursement agreement that is recorded as a lien, and the lien becomes due in full when the property is sold. We do not know whether New Britain has adopted that option, so ask the city.

Chapter 204 also has sections on collection by suit, on receivership of rents for delinquent taxes and on taxes that become uncollectible after fifteen years. If you are far behind, talk to a lawyer before assuming any of those apply.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit affect New Britain houses?
sections.html:
Route 9 is the main expressway and connects the city to Hartford through I-84 and I-91 and south to Middletown and Old Saybrook. Interstate 84 clips the northwest corner. Connecticut Transit runs local buses, and downtown New Britain is the southern terminus of CTfastrak, a bus rapid transit line to Hartford's Union Station. Other CTfastrak stops are on East Main Street and East Street, near Central Connecticut State University.

The nearest Amtrak and CTrail Hartford Line station is in neighboring Berlin. Bradley International Airport and Tweed New Haven Airport are the closest commercial airports. Buyers who commute to Hartford or work at the university often search near the busway stops.

New Britain has a mayor and council form of government. Bobby Sanchez is listed as mayor, and a 15-member Common Council sits alongside the mayor. Erin Stewart served as mayor from 2013 to 2025.

The city's motto, "Industry fills the hive and enjoys the honey," reflects its manufacturing past. CTfastrak began operating in March 2015, and the city hosts the New Britain Bees collegiate summer baseball team at New Britain Stadium and Hartford City FC soccer at the university field. The New Britain Museum of American Art is described as the oldest art museum in the country devoted to American art, and Walnut Hill has a rose garden with more than 800 roses.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods and schools define New Britain?
sections.html:
New Britain has the largest Polish population of any Connecticut city, and its Broad Street area has been officially designated Little Poland since 2008. Wikipedia says the community has helped revitalize that area. Downtown New Britain and Walnut Hill Park are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

The Consolidated School District of New Britain runs the public schools, and New Britain High School is the city's public high school. Higher education includes Central Connecticut State University and Charter Oak State College. Sacred Heart School is the Catholic elementary school.

sections.h2: Can you sell a New Britain house with taxes owed?
sections.html: Yes. A sale closes after the title company confirms what is owed and pays it from the proceeds. The sequence that works best is simple: get a written payoff from the Tax Collector, ask your attorney to check for liens, and decide whether to repair and list or sell as-is. A cash purchase suits owners whose house needs work, has tenants or sits in probate, though you should always read an offer closely and compare it to the alternatives.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in New Britain?
faqs.a: The city's Tax Collector bills and collects it, and the Assessor sets the assessment. Use the city's online payments page or call the office for balances.
About 13.4 square miles and 74,135 residents at the 2020 census.

faqs.q: Can New Britain reduce tax for someone who cannot pay?
faqs.a: Connecticut Section 12-124 lets a city abate taxes or interest for poor persons who are unable to pay, subject to approval. Ask the Tax Collector what New Britain offers.

faqs.q: What happens to an abatement lien when I sell?
faqs.a: Under Section 12-124a, a recorded reimbursement lien becomes due in full upon sale or transfer of the property, if the city adopted that option.

faqs.q: Can I sell my New Britain house for cash with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Back taxes are paid from the proceeds at closing, so ask for a written payoff before you accept an offer.
